title: Christopher Nolan Says There Is a ‘Fundamental Flaw’ With Amateur Film Criticism: ‘To Identify the Mechanism Does Not Invalidate the Mechanism’
content:
ByMya Copeland

Critics have said their piece aboutChristopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” and now he is saying his piece about them.

While on “The Odyssey” press tour, the director spokewith podcaster Zhong Shuabout “a fundamental flaw of film criticism” he sees with amateur critics.

“The criticism that’s often leveled at movies in general is, ‘Oh, the character has to be made sympathetic, so the character is manipulated in different ways or changed in different ways,’” he said. “And that’s a fundamental flaw of film criticism in a way, or storytelling criticism. Because to be able to identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism.”

He added, “I’m thinking more of amateur criticism, because they feel they’ve identified the mechanism, they feel that it invalidates it. That can be true of certain elements, and film grammar, film language evolves with that. So when a trope becomes too familiar to an audience, then it has to be changed. But we do, as filmmakers, avail ourselves of that common language. We build on that understanding. Our audience has seen many films and they understand that language.”

There has been plenty of online discourse surrounding “The Odyssey,” which has grossed nearly $1 billion worldwide after three weekends in theaters and earned a 94% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. One critic who was notably unimpressed with Nolan’s work was Emily Wilson, an “Odyssey” translator whom the director credited as an inspiration for his adaptaion of the Greek epic. Shewrote in a reviewfor the London Review of Books that Nolan’s take was “psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth.”

Author Joyce Carol Oates latercame to Nolan’s defense, writing on social media that Wilson was speaking in the “crude language of MAGA folks” in her blistering critique.
title_zh: 克里斯多福·諾蘭(Christopher Nolan)表示，業餘電影評論存在「根本缺陷」： 「識別機制並不會使該機制失效。」
content_zh:
由Mya Copeland報導

評論家們對克里斯多福·諾蘭(Christopher Nolan)的《奧德賽》(The Odyssey)已經發表了看法，而現在他也對他們的評價做出了回應。

在《奧德賽》(The Odyssey)的宣傳巡演中，這位導演與播客主持人鍾書(Zhong Shu)談到了他所看到的業餘評論家的“電影批評的根本缺陷”。

“對於電影的批評通常是這樣的：‘哦，角色必須讓人同情，所以角色以不同的方式被操控或改變，’”他說。“這在某種程度上是電影批評或敘事批評的根本缺陷。因為能夠識別機制並不會使這個機制失效。”

他補充道：“我更關注的是業餘批評，因為他們覺得自己已經識別了這個機制，並認為這使其失效。這對某些元素來說可能是正確的，而電影語法、電影語言也隨之演變。因此，當一個老套對觀眾來說變得過於熟悉時，它就必須被改變。但作為電影製作人，我們確實利用了這種共同語言。我們在這種理解的基礎上構建。我們的觀眾看過許多電影，並理解這種語言。”

圍繞《奧德賽》(The Odyssey)的在線討論已經不少，該片在上映三個週末後全球票房接近10億美元，並在爛番茄(Rotten Tomatoes)上獲得94%的評分。一位對諾蘭(Christopher Nolan)的作品特別不以為然的評論家是艾米莉·威爾遜(Emily Wilson)，她是《奧德賽》(The Odyssey)的翻譯者，導演將她視為他改編這部希臘史詩的靈感來源。她在《倫敦書評》(London Review of Books)的一篇評論中寫道，諾蘭的詮釋具有“心理、情感、政治和倫理的深度”。

作家喬伊斯·卡羅爾·奧茲(Joyce Carol Oates)隨後為諾蘭(Christopher Nolan)辯護，在社交媒體上寫道，威爾遜(Emily Wilson)在她尖銳的批評中使用了“美國優先(MAGA)人士的粗俗語言”。
